title: Beyond End-to-End Recovery: Towards a Better Understanding of LLM Steganography via Rolewise Decomposition
abstract: arXiv:2610.30516v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In large language model (LLM) steganography, an encoder hides a private message in an otherwise ordinary response, as text transmitted to a decoder, who attempts to recover it. The success of this private-message transmission is commonly measured through end-to-end (E2E) recovery, which checks whether the decoder correctly reconstructs the private message. However, E2E recovery cannot distinguish encoding failures from decoding failures or reveal how the private message is represented in the encoder's transmitted text. To address these limitations, we introduce a rolewise decomposition framework that separately examines how private messages are represented in encoder transmitted texts, what decoders recover, and what deterministic verification can establish. Across 7,200 encoder responses, we identify 168 verifiable encodings missed by decoders and 706 responses containing private messages reconstructed through word-length or token-ini

translated_title: 超越端到端恢复：通过角色分解更好地理解大语言模型隐写术
translated_abstract: 在大语言模型（LLM）隐写术中，编码器将一条私密信息隐藏在看似普通的回复中，并将文本传输给解码器，由解码器尝试恢复该信息。这种私密信息传输的成功通常通过端到端（E2E）恢复来衡量，即检查解码器是否正确重构了私密信息。然而，端到端恢复无法区分编码失败与解码失败，也无法揭示私密信息在编码器传输文本中的表示方式。为了解决这些局限性，我们引入了一个按角色分解的框架，分别考察私密信息在编码器传输文本中的表示方式、解码器实际恢复出的内容，以及确定性验证能够确立什么。在7,200个编码器回复中，我们识别出168个被解码器遗漏的可验证编码，以及706个包含通过词长或词元初始字母等方式重构私密信息的回复。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个按角色分解的评估框架，将大语言模型隐写术的评估从单一的端到端恢复拆解为编码表示、解码恢复和确定性验证三个独立环节，从而能够区分编码失败与解码失败，并揭示私密信息在传输文本中的隐藏表示方式。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a rolewise decomposition framework that breaks down LLM steganography evaluation beyond end-to-end recovery into separate analyses of encoding representation, decoder recovery, and deterministic verification, enabling the distinction between encoding and decoding failures and revealing how private messages are represented in transmitted texts.
